blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Seafloor spreading was proposed by Harry Hess to explain oceanic crust formation.
New crust forms at divergent boundaries and gradually shifts away from oceanic ridges.
Molten material rises and emerges directly at the ridges.
Magnetic striping patterns on the ocean floor provide critical confirmation of spreading.
The age of oceanic crust increases with distance from the central ridges.
Harry Hess is credited with proposing the seafloor spreading theory.
Seafloor spreading takes place at divergent boundaries, not convergent boundaries.
Magnetic striping on the ocean floor serves as key proof for seafloor spreading.
Older oceanic crust is found farther away from ridges, while younger crust is near the ridge.

blocks.content: • Magnetic striping on the ocean floor confirms spreading.
• Older crust is found farther from ridges.
